youtube.title: Why Is Australia So Empty?
youtube.description:
Why is Australia empty when it covers almost as much ground as the lower 48 US states? About 85 percent of the Australia population lives within 50 kilometres of the sea, while the centre holds fewer people than many small towns. This map explains the Great Dividing Range rain shadow, the outback and a century of plans that failed to move Australians inland.

This episode follows the map: the rain shadow of the Great Dividing Range, the Blue Mountains barrier of 1788 to 1813, Goyder's Line of 1865, the telegraph and railway lines that crossed the interior without filling it, Canberra's 100-mile rule and the Albury-Wodonga growth centre. Then the case for spreading Australians out, the strongest case for letting the coastal cities grow, and three changes that could redraw the map: the north, the rising sea and the move to the regions.

{CHAPTERS}

youtube.title_before: Why Australia Is Empty: 85% Live on the Edge of a 7.7 Million km² Land

sources.claim: 85 percent of Australians live within 50 kilometres of the sea
sources.source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Year Book Australia 2004, 'How many people live in Australia's coastal areas?' (2001 Census)

sources.claim: Australia covers 7.7 million square kilometres
sources.source: Geoscience Australia, 'Area of Australia - States and Territories' (7,688,287 km2)

sources.claim: The lower 48 US states cover about 8.1 million square kilometres
sources.source: US Census Bureau, State Area Measurements (contiguous US 8,080,464 km2), 2010

sources.claim: The Northern Territory covers 1.35 million square kilometres with about 250,000 people
sources.source: Geoscience Australia, Area of Australia; ABS National, state and territory population, 2024

sources.claim: Over a third of world iron ore comes from the Pilbara: in 2023 Australia mined about 960 million tonnes, about 38 percent of the world total and the most of any country, almost all of it in the Pilbara, Western Australia
sources.source: US Geological Survey, Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024, Iron Ore (world 2,500 Mt); Geoscience Australia, Australia's Identified Mineral Resources 2023 (Pilbara share of iron ore output)

sources.claim: Australia has roughly 27 million people
sources.source: ABS, National, state and territory population, June 2024 (27.2 million)

sources.claim: Two in three Australians live in the eight capital cities
sources.source: ABS, Regional population 2022-23, released March 2024 (about 67 percent in Greater Capital Cities)

sources.claim: Seven of those eight capitals sit beside the sea; Canberra is the only inland capital
sources.source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard, Greater Capital City Statistical Areas; locations from coordinates: Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Perth, Adelaide, Hobart and Darwin lie on the coast or a tidal estuary, Canberra about 100 km from the nearest coast

sources.claim: Sydney about 5.45 million, Melbourne about 5.21 million, Brisbane 2.71 million, Perth 2.31 million, Adelaide 1.45 million in 2023; Sydney and Melbourne together about 40 percent
sources.source: ABS, Regional population 2022-23 (Greater Capital City Statistical Areas, June 2023; national total 26.6 million)

sources.claim: Darwin has about 150,000 people
sources.source: ABS, Regional population 2022-23 (Greater Darwin)

sources.claim: Sydney to Perth about 3,300 km; Perth to Adelaide about 2,100 km; Darwin closer to Jakarta than to Sydney
sources.source: Great-circle distances computed from city coordinates (Sydney-Perth 3,290 km; Perth-Adelaide 2,130 km; Darwin-Jakarta 2,700 km; Darwin-Sydney 3,150 km)

sources.claim: The Great Dividing Range runs more than 3,500 kilometres
sources.source: Geoscience Australia, 'Mountains' (Landforms), accessed 2026

sources.claim: Mount Kosciuszko is 2,228 metres
sources.source: Geoscience Australia, 'Highest Mountains'

sources.claim: About half of Australia gets less than 300 mm of rain a year
sources.source: Bureau of Meteorology / Geoscience Australia, 'Climate of Australia' (50 percent of the continent under 300 mm)

sources.claim: Sydney averages about 1,213 mm of rain a year; Alice Springs about 283 mm
sources.source: Bureau of Meteorology, climate statistics: Sydney Observatory Hill (066062) and Alice Springs Airport (015590)

sources.claim: Alice Springs is roughly 1,500 km by road from both Adelaide and Darwin
sources.source: Northern Territory Government / Stuart Highway road distances (Alice-Darwin about 1,500 km; Alice-Adelaide about 1,530 km)

sources.claim: About 35 percent of the continent gets so little rain it is effectively desert
sources.source: Geoscience Australia, 'Deserts'

sources.claim: Kati Thanda-Lake Eyre lies about 15 metres below sea level, with no outlet to the sea
sources.source: Geoscience Australia, 'Highest and lowest points'; Lake Eyre Basin Ministerial Forum

sources.claim: The Great Artesian Basin underlies about 22 percent of Australia
sources.source: Geoscience Australia, 'Great Artesian Basin' (about 1.7 million km2)

sources.claim: The Murray-Darling Basin covers about a million square kilometres, produces over a third of Australia's food and is home to about 2.3 million people
sources.source: Murray-Darling Basin Authority, 'Discover the Basin', accessed 2026

sources.claim: Many mine crews work fly-in, fly-out from coastal cities such as Perth
sources.source: Parliament of Western Australia, Education and Health Standing Committee, 'The impact of FIFO work practices on mental health', June 2015

sources.claim: About 2 in 100 Australians live in remote or very remote areas
sources.source: ABS, 2021 Census, Remoteness Areas

sources.claim: About 3.5 people per square kilometre in Australia; about 36 in the United States
sources.source: Derived from ABS 2024 population and Geoscience Australia area; US Census Bureau 2020 Census (93.8 per sq mile)

sources.claim: Aboriginal people have lived here for at least 65,000 years by the dating of Madjedbebe
sources.source: Clarkson et al., 'Human occupation of northern Australia by 65,000 years ago', Nature, July 2017

sources.claim: Other researchers argue the evidence points closer to 50,000 years
sources.source: O'Connell et al., 'When did Homo sapiens first reach Southeast Asia and Sahul?', PNAS, August 2018

sources.claim: More than 250 languages were spoken before 1788
sources.source: AIATSIS, Map of Indigenous Australia and 'Indigenous Australian languages'

sources.claim: Estimates of the 1788 population range from about 315,000 to more than one million
sources.source: ABS, Year Book Australia 2002, 'Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander population'

sources.claim: On 26 January 1788 the First Fleet's eleven ships anchored at Sydney Cove with about 1,400 to 1,500 people, the first European settlement
sources.source: State Library of New South Wales, First Fleet collection; National Museum of Australia, 'Defining Moments: Arrival of the First Fleet'

sources.claim: About 50 kilometres west of Sydney Cove, the sandstone cliffs of the Blue Mountains
sources.source: Great-circle distance computed from coordinates: Sydney Cove (-33.859, 151.211) to the foot of the Blue Mountains escarpment near Emu Plains-Glenbrook (-33.75, 150.64), about 53 km; NSW National Parks and Wildlife Service, 'Blue Mountains National Park' (sandstone escarpment)

sources.claim: The Blue Mountains held the colony to the coastal plain for 25 years; crossed in May 1813 by Blaxland, Lawson and Wentworth
sources.source: National Museum of Australia, 'Defining Moments: Crossing the Blue Mountains'

sources.claim: A road reached Bathurst in 1815, roughly 150 to 160 km west of Sydney in a straight line
sources.source: NSW State Archives, Cox's Road (completed January 1815); straight-line distance computed from coordinates: Sydney CBD (-33.869, 151.209) to Bathurst (-33.419, 149.578) about 159 km, less from Sydney's western edge

sources.claim: In 1844 Charles Sturt set out from Adelaide hoping to find an inland sea; his expedition reached the stony desert now named Sturt Stony Desert
sources.source: State Library of South Australia, 'Charles Sturt's Central Australian Expedition 1844-46'

sources.claim: In 1865 surveyor-general George Goyder mapped a line marking where rainfall was reliable enough to farm
sources.source: State Library of South Australia, 'Goyder's Line'; D. W. Meinig, On the Margins of the Good Earth, 1962

sources.claim: Land beyond the line was opened to wheat farming in the wetter 1870s; many farms were abandoned in the drier 1880s
sources.source: D. W. Meinig, On the Margins of the Good Earth, 1962; SA History Hub, 'Goyder's Line'

sources.claim: Goyder's Line still roughly marks where cropping gives way to grazing in South Australia
sources.source: Primary Industries and Regions SA (PIRSA); SA History Hub, 'Goyder's Line'

sources.claim: The Overland Telegraph Line, completed in 1872, ran about 3,200 km from Adelaide to Darwin through Alice Springs
sources.source: National Archives of Australia, 'Overland Telegraph Line' (completed 22 August 1872)

sources.claim: The Trans-Australian Railway was completed in 1917 with a 478 km straight across the Nullarbor
sources.source: Australian Rail Track Corporation; National Museum of Australia (completed 17 October 1917)

sources.claim: The Adelaide-Darwin railway reached Darwin in 2004
sources.source: AustralAsia Railway Corporation; first freight train arrived in Darwin January 2004

sources.claim: On 1 January 1901 six colonies federated into one country under a new Constitution
sources.source: Commonwealth of Australia Constitution Act 1900 (UK), in force 1 January 1901 by Queen's proclamation; National Archives of Australia, 'Commonwealth of Australia Constitution Act'

sources.claim: Section 125 places the seat of government in New South Wales, not less than 100 miles from Sydney
sources.source: Commonwealth of Australia Constitution Act 1900, section 125

sources.claim: Canberra was chosen in 1908, about 250 km southwest of Sydney and about 100 km from the sea
sources.source: Seat of Government Act 1908; distances computed from coordinates (Sydney-Canberra about 247 km; Canberra-Batemans Bay coast about 105 km)

sources.claim: The ACT holds about 470,000 people; Canberra is the largest inland city
sources.source: ABS, National, state and territory population, 2023-24

sources.claim: In 1973 Albury-Wodonga was chosen as a national growth centre aiming for about 300,000 people by 2000
sources.source: Albury-Wodonga Development Act 1973; National Archives of Australia, Department of Urban and Regional Development records

sources.claim: The 2021 census counted fewer than 100,000 people in Albury-Wodonga
sources.source: ABS, 2021 Census QuickStats, Albury-Wodonga Significant Urban Area

sources.claim: The Regional Australia Institute aims for 11 million people in regional Australia by 2032
sources.source: Regional Australia Institute, 'Regionalisation Ambition 2032', 2022

sources.claim: In 2020-21 capital cities lost a net 43,000 people to the regions through internal migration, a record
sources.source: ABS, Regional population 2020-21, released March 2022

sources.claim: 0.2 percent of Australia's land produces about 80 percent of its economic activity
sources.source: Grattan Institute, 'Mapping Australia's economy: cities as engines of prosperity', July 2014

sources.claim: Perth draws close to half its drinking water from two desalination plants
sources.source: Water Corporation (WA), 'Desalination', accessed 2026

sources.claim: The Snowy Mountains Scheme was built 1949-1974 by more than 100,000 people from over 30 countries
sources.source: Snowy Hydro Limited, 'Our history'

sources.claim: The scheme releases on average about 2,100 GL a year to the Murray and Murrumbidgee
sources.source: Snowy Hydro Limited, 'Water' (average annual releases)

sources.claim: Snowy water generates hydropower on the way, then supplies irrigation in the south-east's Murray and Murrumbidgee valleys
sources.source: Snowy Hydro Limited, 'Our history' and 'Water'; Murray-Darling Basin Authority, 'Snowy Mountains Scheme'

sources.claim: The north covers about 40 percent of the land and holds about 1.3 million people, about five percent
sources.source: Australian Government, 'Our North, Our Future: White Paper on Developing Northern Australia', June 2015

sources.claim: Darwin averages about 1,700 mm of rain, nearly all in the wet season
sources.source: Bureau of Meteorology, climate statistics, Darwin Airport (014015)

sources.claim: The Ord River scheme dammed Lake Argyle in 1971
sources.source: Water Corporation WA / Government of Western Australia, 'Ord River Dam' (completed 1971)

sources.claim: NAIF set up in 2016 with $5 billion, raised to $7 billion in 2021
sources.source: Northern Australia Infrastructure Facility Act 2016; NAIF Amendment Act 2021

sources.claim: A 2009 federal report put between 157,000 and 247,600 existing homes at risk under a 1.1 m sea-level rise, a high-end scenario for 2100
sources.source: Department of Climate Change, 'Climate Change Risks to Australia's Coast', 2009
